messages:
Maya (support): Hey team — customer (acct: acme-inc) opened a high-priority ticket: embeddings API returning "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024" when they batch 8 texts. They switched from rwd-embed-lite -> rwd-embed-pro and started batching. Error snippet: `{"error":"dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024"}`. Repro steps attached by customer: curl to /v1/embeddings with model=rwd-embed-pro and payload as an array of 8 strings.

Jordan (eng-ml): Thanks Maya. Two quick checks: 1) are they mixing models in the same batch? 2) can they paste the exact request body?

Maya (support): They said they updated model param on headers but their client lib (internal) still uses cached model id for some calls. Here's the payload they sent (redacted):

```\n{\n  "model": "rwd-embed-pro",\n  "input": ["text A","text B", ... "text H"]\n}\n```

No obvious mixing but I suspect the client might be batching calls to different endpoints or pre-allocating a numpy array with shape (8,1024).

Carlos (sre): Fender-check: if server expects 1536 and they send a 1024-length vector (e.g., precomputed or wrong client lib), we return that mismatch. But also batching across different models can happen if middleware merges requests. Can we get request_id or raw request body from logs?

Maya (support): I grabbed the request_id from the customer: rq_01G9X7Z8. Not in logs due to sampling, asked for full header X-Request-ID.

Jordan (eng-ml): Short runbook: 1) confirm model -> dimension mapping (rwd-embed-lite=1024, rwd-embed-pro=1536). 2) verify client isn't precomputing vectors or reshaping arrays. 3) replicate with curl using the exact model and multiple inputs. If mismatch persists, we need a server-side improvement to return which model expectation triggered the error. I'll open ENG-ML ticket.

Priya (docs): We should add a small FAQ entry: "why am I seeing dimension mismatch" with table mapping model names to dims + example payloads for batching. Also show python + curl examples. I'll take this if eng confirms mapping.

Sam (support-manager): Prioritize. Customer is on dedicated, so SLA is stricter. Escalate to prod oncall if we can reproduce. Maya please collect: a minimal repro curl, model name, batch size, and which SDK version they use.

Maya (support): Collected SDK version: rwd-sdk v0.9.3 and custom js client that does batching. Customer says sending JSON with `input: [...]` and they see mismatch only after switching to rwd-embed-pro. They can repro locally if they force the client to use rwd-embed-lite id.

Jordan (eng-ml): Action plan (short):
- Step A: try curl repro with model=rwd-embed-pro and same texts. If we get same error -> likely client is sending precomputed embeddings (shape mismatch) OR middleware changed model ID.
- Step B: if repro fails on our curl, ask customer for raw HTTP request capture (headers + body).
- Step C: Add server-side validation to include expected dim and received dim in error and log model id. Ticket ENG-ML-1337 opened.

Jordan (eng-ml): Quick curl repro to run locally: 
```\ncurl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings \\\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \\\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\n  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-pro","input":["hello","world","how are you"]}'\n```

Carlos (sre): Also check payload size. If a custom proxy concatenates small requests into one HTTP body but keeps older model metadata, it can cause mismatched dims at the runtime. If batching > 64 items we sometimes see memory pressure and partial failures; recommend keeping batch <= 64 or <1MB payload for now. We'll instrument more metrics.

Maya (support): Customer responded with raw request id and full headers (pasted privately). Looks like the proxy rewrites model header for some requests to rwd-embed-lite to save cost. So they were mixing models inside the same proxy-batched HTTP request. That explains it.

Sam (support-manager): Good find. Immediate remediation: ask customer to stop proxy rewriting model id, or ensure proxy aggregates only same-model calls. Offer to whitelist them temporarily while they fix the proxy. Also offer to rate-limit/segregate.

Priya (docs): I'll add an FAQ blurb: 
- Problem: "dimension mismatch: expected X got Y"
- Cause: mixing different embedding models in the same batched request or sending precomputed vectors of wrong size.
- Fixes: ensure consistent `model` param per request, confirm SDK version, example curl/python showing correct shape for batching.

Jordan (eng-ml): For longer-term, we should: 1) surface model->dim mapping in the API docs (table + JSON sample), 2) update the error payload to include both expected_dim and received_dim, and model_id used to compute expected_dim. Created ENG-ML-1337.

Priya (docs): I'll create DOCS-211 to add the mapping table + example code + tip about proxies.

Maya (support): I'll update the customer: root cause is proxy mixing model IDs. Proposed next steps: 1) stop mixed-model batching, 2) resend the batched request with single model, or 3) switch back to single-item calls until proxy fixed. Also offered a temporary support ticket for fast-tracked assistance. Customer accepted.

Carlos (sre): I'll add a quick metric on "embedding_dim_mismatch" occurrences and log model_id + client_app to help catch future cases. ENG-SRE-709 created.

Maya (support): Closing loop: customer ran a single-model batch and error gone. They want better docs and friendlier error messages.

Sam (support-manager): Assignments:
- Maya -> follow-up note in ticket SUP-4829 and confirm closure.
- Priya -> DOCS-211 (add FAQ and mapping).
- Jordan -> ENG-ML-1337 (error payload + validation).
- Carlos -> ENG-SRE-709 (metric + alert).

Priya (docs): I'll add the FAQ and small runbook snippet: 
```\nWhen you get dimension mismatch:\n1) check model name -> expected dim (table)\n2) ensure payload.input is an array of strings (not precomputed vectors)\n3) if batching via proxy, ensure the proxy doesn't rewrite model id or mix requests\n4) try single-item calls to isolate\n```

Jordan (eng-ml): One more note: suggest we add a runtime sanity-check that rejects mixed-model batched HTTP requests with a clearer 400 and message. I'll include that in ENG-ML-1337.

Maya (support): Customer asked for a short KB link. Priya, can you ping when DOCS-211 is live so I can send link?

Priya (docs): Will do. Target EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

EmbedBot (system): Ticket SUP-4829 created and linked to ENG-ML-1337, DOCS-211, ENG-SRE-709.

Sam (support-manager): Thanks everyone. Good quick triage and handoff. Closing thread once DOCS-211 published and ENG-ML patch merges. :white_check_mark:
